inputs.label: Number of sales territories
inputs.definition: Sales territories funded last year, filled or open; a territory is a slot in your coverage design, not a person.
inputs.original_text: Enter the number of open sales territories you had last year. This is not based on individual people, so if someone has left the company, but the territory is still open, count that as a sales territory.

inputs.label: Average revenue per sales transaction
inputs.definition: Average revenue per closed contract. Enter it directly, or leave blank and the model divides revenue by contracts (lines below).
inputs.where: Finance: revenue ÷ contracts, or CRM closed-won report
inputs.original_text: This is the average deal size for your company. For this simple analysis, you can get this figure by dividing your revenue by total number of contracts. For more detailed analysis, we recommend that you break things down into product lines, services offerings, and sales channels. You should also separate new client revenue from upselling your installed base. For professional services, credit the total esimated hours for a project towards one sales transaction.

inputs.label: Number of contracts last year
inputs.definition: Contracts closed in the year.
inputs.original_text: Number of contracts last year

inputs.label: Revenue from those contract
inputs.definition: Revenue recognized from those contracts.
inputs.original_text: Revenue from those contract

inputs.label: Average fully loaded salary
inputs.definition: Fully loaded cost of one salesperson per year. Enter it directly, or leave blank and the model computes salary × (1 + load rate).
inputs.where: Payroll and benefits ledger, quota-carrying roles only
inputs.original_text: To help develop the most effective market development effort, we must better understand our cost of sales and what drives them. Right now we are focusing on the salaries of the sales team only. Do not count salaries of non-quota carrying managers, sales engineers, or other executives. Your CFO should know what your benefits load rate is. This metric assumes a fully loaded resource (insurance, 401K, FICA, allocation of overhead, etc).

inputs.label: Average salary per sales rep
inputs.definition: Average base salary of a quota-carrying salesperson.
inputs.original_text: Average salary per sales rep

inputs.label: Corporate load rate
inputs.definition: Benefits and payroll taxes as a share of base salary, e.g. 0.23.
inputs.original_text: Corporate load rate

inputs.label: Average travel costs per rep
inputs.definition: Travel and entertainment per salesperson per year. Enter it directly, or leave blank and the model builds it from the trip lines below.
inputs.where: T&E ledger for quota-carrying salespeople ÷ salespeople
inputs.original_text: Most CFO's track overall travel expenses and try to reduce costs by limiting per diems, hotel expenses, etc. However, the real driver is a sales call. Sales people only incur these travel costs on the road. The best way to reduce travel costs is to get a better return out of each sales trip. Oftentimes, sales people will go on multiple client site visits to gain information easily gathered over the phone, or to have meetings with buyers who lack the right marketing materials to decide to buy your solution. Below are the elements of a sales trip. Estimate the costs assumed for each sales trip. Again, only assume the cost of a single sales person. Sales engineers and other costs are too complex for simple analysis.

inputs.label: Travel (air fare, train, mileage round trip)
inputs.definition: Air, train or mileage, round trip, one person.
inputs.original_text: Travel (air fare, train, mileage round trip)

inputs.label: Cabs, tolls, car rentals (etc)
inputs.definition: Ground transport per trip.
inputs.original_text: Cabs, tolls, car rentals (etc)

inputs.label: Meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) per day
inputs.definition: Meals per day away.
inputs.original_text: Meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) per day

inputs.label: Lodging (per night average room expense)
inputs.definition: Average room cost per night.
inputs.original_text: Lodging (per night average room expense)

inputs.label: Days gone per trip
inputs.definition: Days away per trip.
inputs.original_text: Days gone per trip

inputs.label: Entertainment (client dinners, lunch, movies, etc.) per each trip
inputs.definition: Client entertainment per trip.
inputs.original_text: Entertainment (client dinners, lunch, movies, etc.) per each trip

inputs.label: Trips per year
inputs.definition: Sales trips per salesperson per year.
inputs.original_text: Trips per year

inputs.label: Commission
inputs.definition: Commission as a share of revenue, e.g. 0.08.
inputs.where: Compensation plan, or commissions paid ÷ revenue
inputs.original_text: Commissions are the most logical and well understood driver of variable sales costs. Simply enter your sales forces average commission. Again, for simple analysis - just use an average. This model can be modified to accommodate your whole compensation plan.

inputs.label: Number of pipeline opportunities manageable at one time
inputs.definition: The most qualified opportunities one salesperson can hold and advance well at the same time.
inputs.where: Sales leadership; test against CRM load per salesperson
inputs.original_text: One driver of sales force inefficiency is the amount of NON-selling time spent by sales people. Some companies estimate as much at 50% of their time is invested in "non-selling" activities. Our studies reveal that a larger portion of that time in spend in activitity that isn't value-added to customers. The best way to financially measure that impact is by monitoring the number of accounts any given sales person can effectively manage at the same time. The greater amount of time you allow your sales people to sell - the more opportunities they can work in a given year.

inputs.label: Length of sales cycle (in months)
inputs.definition: Months from qualified opportunity to signature, won deals.
inputs.original_text: Tracks how long from when a qualified opportunity enters the pipeline to when it closes as a sale. Your sales process may have many steps, so for simplicity track the time it takes from first meeting to the date the agreement is received by accounting. Most organizations do not track this information, so if you do not have the data - make an estimate. The single greatest impact you can have on your business is to shorten your sales cycle times.

inputs.label: Sales ramp up time (in months)
inputs.definition: Months until a new salesperson reaches average productivity.
inputs.original_text: How long does it take to get a new sales person up to speed to where they are operating at maximum efficiency? Most high tech companies do a good job of training sales people on what their products are, but do very little to help them understand WHY the product is important or how to sell it. This leads to lengthy "ramp up" times. We recommend getting this figure from a sales manager.

inputs.label: close rate
inputs.definition: Won ÷ (won + lost) qualified opportunities, e.g. 0.25.
inputs.original_text: This certainly can mean a lot of things to different people. Here we want to understand the effectiveness of how well your organization manages the sales process from first sales meeting to eventual close. Please estimate the percentage of all of the pipeline opportunities that your organization has worked that have resulted in an executed agreement.

inputs.label: Total Sales Overhead and Marketing Costs
inputs.definition: Total of the two sections below. Enter directly only if you cannot split it.
inputs.original_text: Our goal with this exercise is to assess how well your company is is utilizing its sales and marketing assets. To do this, we have to examine all of the associated costs that are related to sales and marketing performance. This will help you put these investments in the right context and determine the effectiveness of these investments.

inputs.label: Sales Overhead Costs
inputs.definition: Non-variable cost of running the sales organization. Enter directly, or leave blank and the model sums the lines below.
inputs.original_text: This tracks all of the non-variable costs associated with running a sales organization, and includes executive salaries, sales support, training, and performance plans.
